content_html:
Your codebase remembers why.

Know which agent and model wrote every line, and the intent, prompts, decisions and checks behind it. Sploom lives beside git, not instead of it: run sploom init once, then keep using git as usual.

Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Devin CLI, Grok Build, Goose and Cline, and with any MCP-capable agent through sploom mcp-serve.

  • sploom why src/auth.rs:142: which prompt, agent, model and intent produced this code, which constraints apply, and which checks passed.
  • sploom rewind --green: go back to the last state where the checks passed, between commits. sploom forward undoes it.
  • sploom context "…": gives the next agent the relevant symbols, constraints and decisions, within a token budget. Runs on your machine: the first use downloads a small embedding model (about 130 MB), then it works offline.

Website: sploom.pages.dev · Design: RFC-0002

Install

Requires Rust and git.

cargo install --git https://github.com/vrannang1/sploom sploom sploomd

This installs two binaries: sploom, the CLI, and sploomd, a small background file watcher.

Turn capture on

cd your-project
sploom init

sploom init is the only setup step. It:

  • records a baseline of your current commit, so sploom why works immediately
  • installs git hooks: commit, push, pull, amend and rebase carry provenance (your existing hooks keep working)
  • asks which coding agents on your machine to connect, and adds Sploom's hooks to each one's project settings. Nothing changes without a yes (see Agents)
  • imports your teammates' Sploom notes if the remote has any
  • starts sploomd

Check it at any time. The first line of sploom status tells you whether capture is on:

Capture: ON  (Claude Code ✓ · Codex ✓ · git hooks ✓ · sploomd ✓)

sploom hooks remove takes everything out again.

How it works with git

You run Sploom does
git commit Records a weave of exactly what you committed, credited to the agent run that wrote it, and attaches a git note
git commit --amend, git rebase Rewritten commits keep their provenance
git push Also pushes refs/notes/sploom, in the background. It never slows or fails the push
git pull, git checkout Imports teammates' notes and new commits

What stays on your machine (.sploom/, never committed): tool output, the snapshots between commits, the vector index, and the readable copy of prompts.

What travels with git (refs/notes/sploom): intents, requirements, constraints, decisions, which agent and model wrote each change, verification results, and prompts, encrypted to your team's SSH keys.

Prompts are encrypted to your team's SSH keys

Prompts are shared with the people who should read them, and nobody else. Each prompt is encrypted with age to the SSH public keys listed in the repository's committed .sploomkeys file. These are the same keys you already use with git. GitHub or GitLab only ever store ciphertext.

sploom keys add github:alice   # Alice's keys from github.com/alice.keys (gitlab:… works too)
git add .sploomkeys && git commit -m "Alice can read our prompts"
sploom keys list               # who can read; which of your keys are used

sploom init adds your own key. A teammate's sploom why decrypts with their own SSH private key, asking for its passphrase if it has one, and keeps the readable copy locally. Someone who isn't listed still sees who wrote the code, which model, the intent and the decisions, but not the prompt. Supported keys are ssh-ed25519 and ssh-rsa. To keep prompts on your machine, set share_prompts = "off" under [bridge] in .sploom/config.toml. "plain" shares them redacted but readable by anyone with the repository.

Commands
sploom why <file:line | symbol> Why this code exists
sploom log, sploom status Weave history; is capture on
sploom rewind [--green | <weave>], sploom forward Journaled, reversible restore
sploom context "<query>" Hybrid retrieval for the next agent
sploom intent, sploom guard, sploom decision Intents, guardrails (constraints), decisions
sploom verify, sploom impact "<change>" Verification evidence; impact analysis
sploom session start "<what>" [--worktree] Name a piece of work; optional isolated worktree
sploom merge, sploom rebase Three-level merge with an audit trail
sploom bridge push | pull | import Manual git-notes sync; import existing history
sploom privacy purge, sploom gc Retention and garbage collection
sploom mcp-serve MCP tools for any agent
sploom hooks install | remove | status Manage the integrations
sploom keys list | add | remove | unlock Who can read shared prompts (SSH keys in .sploomkeys)

Agents

Sploom captures each agent through that agent's own hooks: prompts, file edits, check commands and turns, credited to the agent and model that made them.

Agent Hooks in Prompts Edits & checks Model
Claude Code .claude/settings.local.json ✓ ✓ ✓
Codex .codex/hooks.json ✓ ✓ ✓
Cursor .cursor/hooks.json ✓ ✓ ✓
Gemini CLI .gemini/settings.json ✓ ✓ ✓
Copilot CLI .github/hooks/sploom.json ✓ ✓ not reported by Copilot
Devin CLI .devin/hooks.v1.json ✓ ✓ not reported by Devin
Grok Build .grok/hooks/sploom.json ✓ ✓ not reported by Grok Build
Goose ~/.agents/plugins/sploom/ (per user) ✓ ✓ not reported by Goose
Cline .clinerules/hooks/<Event> ✓ ✓ not reported by Cline 
sploom hooks status                         # which agents are found and connected
sploom hooks install --agents codex,cursor  # connect specific agents
sploom hooks remove                         # disconnect everything

Codex runs new project hooks only after you approve them once with /hooks, Grok Build after /hooks-trust, and Gemini CLI asks you to trust them. Cline needs "Enable Hooks" switched on in its VS Code settings. Goose loads hooks only from plugins, so Sploom installs a small per-user plugin that does nothing outside Sploom repositories. Devin's cloud sessions run on Cognition's machines; Sploom sees their work as commits (untracked), and Devin CLI runs are captured fully. Sploom keeps the hook files it creates out of git (.git/info/exclude), and leaves your own settings in them untouched.

An edit that no connected agent reported, whether made by hand or by an agent that isn't connected, is shown as untracked. It is never credited to you or to the wrong agent. Any other MCP-capable agent can use Sploom's tools through sploom mcp-serve. See hooks/README.md.

Privacy

Secrets are redacted before anything is written to disk. The patterns cover cloud and API keys, tokens, JWTs, private keys, credentials in URLs and .env secrets. Prompts and tool output are stored apart from the graph, can be encrypted (XChaCha20-Poly1305) and follow a retention policy you choose. Everything runs locally. The only data that leaves your machine is in the git notes you push, and the prompts in them are encrypted to your team's SSH keys.
